newsitem.title: TURKEY: IMF offers support to Turkey's economy -- paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF offers support to Turkey's economy -- paper.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has said it is ready to give Turkey's new government its support in implementing economic reforms, the Turkish Milliyet daily quoted economy minister Gunes Taner as saying on Tuesday.
"The IMF is ready to assist the economic programme of the Turkish authorities," the paper quoted a letter sent by the IMF's Stanley Fisher to Taner as saying.
"We will open discussions on the programme to be prepared," the letter said.
Milliyet said the talks between the Turkish government and the IMF would take place in Hong Kong in September.

The IMF, after a visit to Turkey in April, urged Ankara to adopt a comprehensive programme of stabilisation policies and structural reforms to lower inflation -- currently around 80 percent -- and set the economy on a path of sustainable growth.

Turkey's left-right coalition which came to power at the end of June has said it has taken up some of the measures earlier recommended by the IMF, including a protocol between the treasury and central bank to cooperate against inflation.
